goal: Make canonical backlog persistence deterministic and idempotent so readiness and reconciliation do not create non-semantic formatting, key-order, or revision churn.
scope: control-plane JSON persistence semantic no-op detection
stable backlog serialization without sorted-key reordering
readiness refresh revision changes only when canonical state semantically changes
regression coverage for repeated refresh and reconciliation cycles
preservation of existing backlog task semantics and history
out_of_scope: backlog task redesign or history migration
changes to Apex Core Task, Attempt, authority, or verification semantics
discarding unexplained local artifacts or unrelated work
architecture_constraints: backlog revision advances only for semantic canonical-state changes
existing task semantics, evidence states, dependencies, and history remain preserved
acceptance_criteria: semantically equal JSON persistence does not rewrite existing bytes
actual persistence does not reorder existing backlog keys through sorted-key serialization
repeated refresh_readiness calls leave backlog bytes and revision unchanged after convergence
regression tests cover repeated refresh/reconciliation cycles
existing backlog semantics and operational history remain unchanged
validation: canonical backlog and Passport JSON validation
focused control-plane persistence and readiness tests
repository-wide Python tests and documentation validation
git diff --check and protected PR CI gate
